INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('profile-images', 'profile-images', true) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING. PUBLIC bucket for user profile images.

object_name: Users can view all profile images
detail: FOR SELECT, no TO clause (default: applies to all roles). USING (bucket_id = 'profile-images'). Anyone can read any object in the profile-images bucket.

object_name: Users can upload their own profile image
detail: FOR INSERT, no TO clause (default: all roles). WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'profile-images' AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]). Upload allowed only into a top-level folder named after the uploader's own auth.uid().

object_name: Users can update their own profile image
detail: FOR UPDATE, no TO clause (default: all roles). USING (bucket_id = 'profile-images' AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]). No WITH CHECK clause.

object_name: Users can delete their own profile image
detail: FOR DELETE, no TO clause (default: all roles). USING (bucket_id = 'profile-images' AND auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]).

ALTER TABLE public.subsections ADD COLUMN inspection_template_id uuid REFERENCES public.inspection_templates(id). Nullable, no default, no ON DELETE action (defaults to NO ACTION). COMMENT ON COLUMN: 'Links subsection to its inspection template type'.
CREATE INDEX idx_subsections_template_id ON public.subsections(inspection_template_id). Plain btree index.
ALTER TABLE public.inspections ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS json_data jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb. Nullable, default empty JSON object. Stores section/item data for an inspection.
ALTER TABLE public.inspections ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS template_id uuid REFERENCES public.inspection_templates(id). Nullable, no default, no ON DELETE action (defaults to NO ACTION).
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_inspections_template_id ON public.inspections(template_id). Plain btree index.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_inspections_json_data ON public.inspections USING gin(json_data). GIN index over the jsonb column.
FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of ALL subsections rows, for QR code landing pages. Later dropped in 20251016035546.
FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of ALL sites rows. Later dropped in 20251016035546.
FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of ALL clients rows including contact information. Later dropped in 20251016035546.

object_name: Public users can view document categories
detail: FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of all document_categories rows. Later dropped in 20251016035546.

object_name: Public users can view subsection documents
detail: FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of all subsection_documents rows. Later dropped in 20251016035546.

object_name: Public users can view site documents
detail: FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Grants anonymous read of all site_documents rows, for QR code landing pages. Later dropped in 20251016035546.

DELETE FROM public.document_categories WHERE name = '05 Photos'. Removes every '05 Photos' document category row. Any subsection_documents referencing those category rows are affected per the FK's delete behavior (defined elsewhere, not in this batch).

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.site_document_categories: id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY; site_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.sites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; name TEXT NOT NULL; order_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT now().
ALTER TABLE public.site_document_categories ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

object_name: Authenticated users can manage site document categories
detail: FOR ALL, no TO clause (default: all roles). USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated'). No WITH CHECK clause (FOR ALL without WITH CHECK reuses the USING expression for writes).

object_name: Public users can view site document categories
detail: FOR SELECT, no TO clause (default: all roles, including anon). USING (true). Later dropped in 20251016035546.

Conditional DO $$ block: if information_schema.columns has no site_documents.category_id, then ALTER TABLE public.site_documents ADD COLUMN category_id UUID REFERENCES public.site_document_categories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. Nullable, no default.

INSERT INTO public.site_document_categories (site_id, name, order_index) SELECT DISTINCT sd.site_id, sd.category, CASE sd.category WHEN '01 COC' THEN 1 WHEN '02 Manuals' THEN 2 WHEN '03 Line Diagram' THEN 3 WHEN '04 Metering' THEN 4 WHEN '05 Thermal Reports' THEN 5 WHEN '06 Other' THEN 6 ELSE 99 END FROM public.site_documents sd WHERE sd.category IS NOT NULL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Creates per-site category rows from the legacy free-text site_documents.category field.

UPDATE public.site_documents sd SET category_id = sdc.id FROM public.site_document_categories sdc WHERE sd.site_id = sdc.site_id AND sd.category = sdc.name AND sd.category_id IS NULL. Backfills the new FK column by matching on (site_id, category text). Migrates from text categories to FK-based categories.

UPDATE inspection_templates SET category = 'Medium Voltage' WHERE name ILIKE '%miniature substation%' OR name ILIKE '%RMU%' OR name ILIKE '%ring main unit%'. Moves miniature-substation / RMU / ring-main-unit templates into the 'Medium Voltage' category.

INSERT INTO inspection_templates (name, category, description, sections, cover_page, sections_count, pages_count) VALUES ('Site Drawing Inspection', 'Site Drawing', 'Interactive PDF site drawing inspection with pin-based annotations for marking specific locations and adding photos and notes', '[]'::jsonb, '{}'::jsonb, 0, 1). No ON CONFLICT clause — re-running would duplicate the row.
ALTER TABLE public.activity_logs ADD COLUMN user_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. Nullable, no default. Added for per-user access control.

UPDATE public.activity_logs SET user_id = profiles.id FROM public.profiles WHERE activity_logs.user_email = profiles.email. Backfills the new user_id column by matching the legacy user_email text to profiles.email. Rows whose email matches no profile keep user_id NULL — those become invisible under the new SELECT policy and uninsertable under the new INSERT policy.
CREATE INDEX idx_activity_logs_user_id ON public.activity_logs(user_id). Plain btree index.

object_name: Authenticated users can view activity logs
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view activity logs" ON public.activity_logs. Removes the permissive any-authenticated-user SELECT policy.

object_name: Users can view their own activity logs
detail: FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (auth.uid() = user_id). Users see only their own log rows.

object_name: Admins can view all activity logs
detail: FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), 'Admin'::app_role)).

object_name: Authenticated users can insert activity logs
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can insert activity logs" ON public.activity_logs.

object_name: Users can insert their own activity logs
detail: FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id). Inserts must carry the caller's own user_id.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can view all profiles" ON public.profiles. Part of 'CRITICAL SECURITY FIX: Remove Public Access to Sensitive Data'.
FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true). Any authenticated user can read all profiles (for mentions/assignments). Dropped in the next migration 20251016064350.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view clients" ON public.clients. Removes anon read of client contact information; relies on the pre-existing "Authenticated users can view clients" policy.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view sites" ON public.sites.

object_name: Public users can view basic site info for QR codes
detail: FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Despite the name, the expression still exposes ALL rows/columns to anon; migration comment says the app should query only id and name. Dropped in the next migration 20251016064350.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view subsections" ON public.subsections.

object_name: Public users can view basic subsection info for QR codes
detail: FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true). Despite the name, still full-row anon access; comment defers field limiting to the app. Dropped in the next migration 20251016064350.

object_name: Public users can view site documents
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view site documents" ON public.site_documents. Removes anon access entirely; relies on pre-existing "Authenticated users can manage site documents" policy.

object_name: Public users can view subsection documents
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view subsection documents" ON public.subsection_documents. Removes anon access entirely; relies on pre-existing "Authenticated users can manage subsection documents" policy.

object_name: Public users can view document categories
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view document categories" ON public.document_categories. Removes anon access; relies on pre-existing "Authenticated users can manage document categories" policy.

object_name: Public users can view site document categories
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view site document categories" ON public.site_document_categories. Removes the USING (true) SELECT policy created in 20251016021558; relies on "Authenticated users can manage site document categories".
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view profiles" ON public.profiles. Removes the all-authenticated-users profile read created in the previous migration.

object_name: Users can view their own profile
detail: FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (auth.uid() = id). Users can read only their own profile row.
FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (has_role(auth.uid(), 'Admin'::app_role)).

object_name: Authenticated users can view clients (drop + recreate)
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view clients" then CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can view clients" ON public.clients FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated'). Net effect: adds explicit TO authenticated role scoping.

object_name: Authenticated users can create clients (drop + recreate)
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can create clients" then CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can create clients" ON public.clients FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (auth.role() = 'authenticated').

object_name: Authenticated users can update clients (drop + recreate)
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can update clients" then CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can update clients" ON public.clients FOR UPDATE TO authenticated USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated'). No WITH CHECK clause.

object_name: Authenticated users can delete clients (drop + recreate)
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can delete clients" then CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can delete clients" ON public.clients FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated').

object_name: Public users can view basic site info for QR codes
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view basic site info for QR codes" ON public.sites.

object_name: Public QR code access - minimal data only
detail: FOR SELECT TO public USING (true). Despite the name, this is full-row access to ALL roles (TO public, broader than the anon-only policy it replaces). Migration comment says applications should SELECT only id, name for public access.

object_name: Public users can view basic subsection info for QR codes
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Public users can view basic subsection info for QR codes" ON public.subsections.

object_name: Public QR code access - subsection name and ID only
detail: FOR SELECT TO public USING (true). Despite the name, full-row access for all roles; comment says apps should SELECT only id, name, site_id for public QR access.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Anyone can view settings" ON public.settings.

FOR SELECT TO public USING (true). Despite the name, exposes ALL settings columns/rows to all roles; comment says frontend should only fetch company_name, company_logo_url, primary_color for public. Functionally equivalent to the dropped "Anyone can view settings" policy.

object_name: Authenticated users can view all settings
detail: FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated').

object_name: Authenticated users can view import data
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can view import data" ON public.temp_import.

object_name: Authenticated users can insert import data
detail: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Authenticated users can insert import data" ON public.temp_import.

object_name: Only admins can manage import data
detail: FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (has_role(auth.uid(), 'Admin'::app_role)) WITH CHECK (has_role(auth.uid(), 'Admin'::app_role)). temp_import becomes admin-only because it lacks per-user tracking.
ALTER TABLE public.temp_import ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS imported_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id). Nullable, no default, no ON DELETE action. Added for future user-specific policies.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_temp_import_user ON public.temp_import(imported_by). Plain btree index. Migration footer also notes leaked-password protection must be enabled manually in the Supabase dashboard (not a SQL change).
